artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

artifacts.synopsis: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

artifacts.title: Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaints of TE Eliot Lee against Korean Eastern Presbytery (cases 2007-09 and 2007-10). KEP erred when it empowered the Pulpit Commission to act on behalf of the church session without proper consent, and erred when it filed a civil action against TE Lee to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters. The decision affirms the non-hierarchical, voluntary nature of the PCA and its limited jurisdiction in civil matters.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Anthony Dallison appealed his deposition from the office of Teaching Elder by North Florida Presbytery, arguing that presbytery lacked authority to increase his censure from indefinite suspension to deposition without conducting a new trial. The SJC affirmed presbytery's decision, holding that where a teaching elder has confessed guilt under BCO 38-1, presbytery may impose additional censure based on evidence of impenitence without initiating new charges, and such disciplinary discretion is within presbytery's constitutional authority.

artifacts.synopsis: Virgil B. Roberts complained that New River Presbytery delayed dissolving his pastoral relationship after he resigned and the congregation concurred. The SJC sustained the complaint, concluding that Presbytery should have acted on the agreed request rather than withholding dissolution; three commissioners dissented concerning Presbytery's constitutional authority and pastoral discretion.

artifacts.title: Nickoley and Stephens v. Southwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Bruce Nickoley and David Stephens complained against Southwest Presbytery's actions in withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving a pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of a local church session. The SJC denied the complaint, affirming that the Presbytery correctly determined it lacked constitutional authority to suspend the session or act as a 'Session pro tem' without congregational consent, and that original jurisdiction over charges against ruling elders rested with the local session.
